cases.why: The simplest declaration there is. If this fails nothing else matters.
288 of 979 real ROOTs quote the session name. The quotes are not part of it.

A quoted name may contain `.` and `-`, and Isabelle session names routinely do (`HOL-Analysis`). Truncating at either renames the session to one that exists, which is the worst kind of wrong answer. This is the valid spelling of the defect found in a hand-rolled parser.
`(slow very_slow)` are build groups, not part of the name; 90 real ROOTs carry them. The group names must not leak into the token stream either.
`in <dir>` says where the theories live, and is not part of the name. 29 real ROOTs use it.
The parent is a session name in its own right and may be qualified.
One ROOT may declare many; 37 real ROOTs do, and HOL/ROOT declares dozens. A reader that stops at the first is wrong about most of them.
cases.root:
session A = HOL +

session B in sub = A +

cases.why: 975 of 979 real ROOTs open with `chapter AFP`. It declares no session.

`sessions` names cross-session dependencies without heap inheritance. 550 real ROOTs have one; its entries are not sessions being declared. Both entries name real distribution sessions, because `isabelle sessions` resolves them and would reject an invented one — a semantic complaint, not a syntactic one, and not what this case is about.
`directories` adds search paths for theory files. 138 real ROOTs use it.
cases.root:
session Probe = HOL +
  directories "sub" "other"
  theories
    Deep

cases.why: `theories [document = false]` — block options belong to the block, not to a theory. 134 real ROOTs write this, and `document` is not a theory.
cases.root:
session Probe = HOL +
  theories [document = false]
    X
    Y

cases.why: How Isabelle addresses a theory in a subdirectory — there is no per-theory `in` clause. 127 real ROOTs do this.
`(global)` marks a theory as globally visible. 13 real ROOTs use it, and `global` is an annotation rather than a second theory.
969 of 979 real ROOTs end with one. Its arguments are file names, not theories.
cases.root:
session Probe = HOL +
  theories
    X
  document_files
    "root.tex"

cases.why: A commented-out session declares nothing.
cases.root:
(* session Retired = HOL + *)
session Live = HOL +

cases.why: The same, spanning lines, which a line-oriented reader cannot see: it has no state carrying `we are inside a comment` from one line to the next, so the declaration looks live.
cases.root:
(*
session Old = HOL +
*)
session Live = HOL +

cases.why: Isabelle's block comments NEST. A non-greedy `(*.*?*)` closes at the first `*)` and re-exposes the tail of the outer comment, resurrecting exactly the declaration that was commented out.
cases.root:
(* outer (* inner *)
session Ghost = HOL +
*)
session Live = HOL +

cases.why: A `description` cartouche is free text and may contain anything, including the word `session` at the start of a line.
cases.root:
session Probe = HOL +
  description \<open>session Ghost = X\<close>

cases.why: 15 real ROOTs write the word `in` inside a `theories` stanza; every one of them is in a comment like this.
cases.root:
session Probe = HOL +
  theories
    (* Basic helpers (in util folder) *)
    X

cases.why: AFP's own `thys/ROOT` is exactly this. It declares no session, and that is not an error — a reader that treats an empty result as a failure reports a broken corpus for a well-formed one.

An empty ROOT declares nothing, and must do so by returning an empty list rather than raising. Callers walk trees full of files they did not write, and a reader that throws on one of them cannot finish the walk.

Isabelle REJECTS this — a session name may not contain spaces or parens. Kept because readers must still agree on what they do with it: the hand-rolled parser truncated at the first space and recorded a build of `Probe (AFP)` against a session named `Probe`, with nothing downstream able to tell. Agreement on malformed input is what stops one reader silently renaming what another built.
cases.isabelle_note: [line 1 of "<ROOT-DIR>/ROOT"] error: session name expected, but string was found: "Probe (AFP)" ^

cases.why: Isabelle REJECTS this — `-` is a symbolic identifier, so a bare name cannot contain one; the quoted form above is the legal spelling. Kept for the same reason: the hand-rolled parser truncated it at the first `.` or `-`, turning it into a different, existing session.
cases.isabelle_note: [line 1 of "<ROOT-DIR>/ROOT"] error: keyword "=" expected, but symbolic identifier was found: - ^

cases.why: An unterminated `(*` swallows the rest of the file, which is what Isabelle's lexer does. Guessing otherwise would mean a typo yields a session list nobody can build.
cases.root:
session A = HOL +
(* oops
session B in sub = A +

cases.why: Parses cleanly and still will not build: two sessions in one directory is a semantic error, not a syntactic one, so `isabelle sessions` rejects a ROOT whose session list this package reads correctly. Kept because it is the distinction the `isabelle` field would otherwise blur — `rejects` means `isabelle build` refuses the file, NOT that a reader which parsed it got the wrong answer. Adding `in sub` to the second declaration is the buildable form, covered above.
cases.root:
session A = HOL +

session B = A +
